why: Template weighting and a use-template tool serve no one of the three big things.
Tap-to-select in Ask is a selection feature outside the review, task-finishing and agent-rules work.
Checkbox and bar styling on task pages is cosmetic and not plainly the session page or task resolution.
A Proposal class that turns decisions into tasks is the sorting of proposed asks into tasks.
A percentage-padding wrapper rule is a layout rule, not one of the three big things.
Framework home grid and layout labels are layout work outside the three big things.
Nested Now sub-cards are a dashboard display change, not the review page or task flow.
A live instance view for AI objects is a code/objects concern; it does not plainly serve the review page or the task loop.
Adding architecture.md to modules is documentation that agents read to know where things go.
Library URLs and tags serve filtering the library, which is not one of the three big things.
Automatic navigation registration is a core/Page navigation concern, not one of the three big things.
Documenting every moving part of the system is the readme and docs work agents depend on to know the rules.
Inbox rail background styling is inbox UI, outside the three big things.
Making the inbox cards and sticky header white is inbox styling.
Making the inbox scroll bar transparent is inbox styling.
A thin inbox scroll bar is inbox styling.
Matching the inbox scroll bar colour is inbox styling.
Inbox rail behaviour on mobile is not the session phone pages in the review work.
A full-width mobile inbox rail is inbox layout, not the session phone pages.
Using the server as an in-memory database for page data is a query architecture question outside the three big things.
Server-side row rendering in ext/Query is outside the three big things.
A Node-versus-browser query benchmark is a performance question not tied to the three big things.
Cutting client subscriptions on session pages for phones makes the mobile session pages that the owner approves from work.
An inbox for every core module is not plainly part of the review page or the task loop.
A live exchange about one inbox item is an inbox feature, not the review page or the task loop.
